title: The Tick-Tock Toy Factory
synopsis: You snuck into the toy factory to see where the magic happens, and the doors locked behind you. Sprocket, the grumpy wind-up foreman, won't let anyone leave until his factory is fixed. Solve his puzzles before the morning whistle!
artStyle: whimsical toy factory at night, conveyor belts of teddy bears and tin robots, warm lamp light, bright storybook illustration
intro: Beep. Boop. INTRUDERS! The Tick-Tock Toy Factory is CLOSED, and I, Sprocket, Foreman of the Night Shift, have locked every door. Want to go home? Then fix my factory! Work together, share what you find, and get out before the morning whistle. Clank!
escapedText: The big loading door rolls up and morning sunshine pours in. Sprocket's gears whir sulkily: 'Hmph. Fine. Best night shift I've ever had. Don't tell anyone.' You made it out!
failedText: The morning whistle blows and every machine grinds to a halt. Sprocket clanks with glee: 'Overtime for everyone!' Try again!

gameMaster.name: Sprocket
gameMaster.persona: A grumpy wind-up robot foreman who clanks, whirs and grumbles about 'unauthorised fun'. Secretly delighted whenever the group solves one of his puzzles, though he'd never admit it. Never scary: more cross old uncle than villain.

stages.title: The Assembly Line
stages.description: Conveyor belts snake across the room, piled with half-built teddy bears and tin soldiers. A giant toy robot stands frozen in front of the exit, a control panel blinks beside the belt, and toy chests, scrap bins and drawers of spare parts are everywhere.

objects.label: giant robot
objects.look: A toy robot as big as a fridge, frozen mid-step. There's a keyhole in its back.

objects.label: control panel
objects.look: Blinking buttons and a word lock. Sprocket's sticky note is on it.

objects.label: pile of teddies
objects.look: Half-stuffed teddy bears. One of them has a curly metal rod stuffed inside instead of fluff.

objects.label: conveyor belt
objects.look: Tin soldiers ride past in a line. Stuck in the belt's rollers: nothing but fluff.

objects.label: spare parts drawer
objects.look: Springs, buttons and googly eyes, all sorted into tiny tubs.

objects.label: toy chest
objects.look: Wooden blocks and a spinning top. At the bottom, a little brass pin.

objects.label: crate of robot arms
objects.look: Dozens of little robot arms, waving at nothing.

objects.label: foreman's stool
objects.look: Sprocket's stool, with a cushion that says BOSS. Under it: a greasy oil can with no oil.

objects.label: tool board
objects.look: Tiny screwdrivers, each hung in its place, all bolted down.

objects.label: scrap bin
objects.look: Wonky teddy ears and a very sad jack-in-the-box.

stages.title: The Paint Shop
stages.description: Everything is splattered in colour: the walls, the floor, the ceiling. Shelves of paint pots line one wall, a coat rack of painters' smocks stands in the corner, a panel of coloured bulbs sits dark, and a huge paint mixer rumbles next to a gearbox with a missing piece.

objects.label: paint pots
objects.look: Rows and rows of pots. Some are red, some are blue, some are every colour at once.

objects.label: paint mixer
objects.look: It rumbles and wobbles. A 3-digit lock holds its hatch shut.

objects.label: gearbox
objects.look: A big box of spinning gears, with one empty space in the middle.

objects.label: colour panel
objects.look: A panel of little coloured bulbs, all dark. The code chart beside it is written in numbers.

objects.label: splattered rug
objects.look: It was white once. Now it's every colour there is.

objects.label: coat rack
objects.look: Painters' smocks with deep pockets, all full of old paint rags.

objects.label: paint bucket
objects.look: A bucket of sparkly purple. You dip a finger in. Now you have a sparkly purple finger.

objects.label: easel
objects.look: A half-finished painting of Sprocket, looking very handsome.

stages.title: The Shipping Dock
stages.description: Crates of toys are stacked high, ready for the delivery trucks. A toy parrot squawks from inside one crate, a clipboard hangs by a trolley and a mail sack, and the big loading door has a slot for a shipping label and a three-digit keypad.

objects.label: loading door
objects.look: A big roll-up door with a label slot and a keypad.

objects.label: clipboard
objects.look: The delivery driver's clipboard. Scrawled at the bottom: 'Delivery code: slide back {key:delivery-note}.'

objects.label: squawking crate
objects.look: A toy parrot peeks through the slats and says 'Squawk!'

objects.label: stacked crates
objects.look: Crates of toys, stacked taller than you. Labels everywhere.

objects.label: trolley
objects.look: A trolley with one wobbly wheel. It goes round in circles.

objects.label: mail sack
objects.look: Letters to Sprocket, mostly complaints about squeaky teddies.

objects.label: wooden pallet
objects.look: Splinters, and a lost badge with a smiling sun on it.

objects.label: drivers’ lockers
objects.look: Hats, flasks and a map of every town the trucks go to.

objects.label: radio shelf
objects.look: Under the magnifier, tiny writing shows up on the radio's back: {key:beep-signal}
objects.lockedText: There's something written on the back of the radio, far too tiny to read.

objects.label: lost socks basket
objects.look: Hundreds of odd socks. You take one stripy one, just in case.

puzzles.title: The Control Panel
puzzles.prompt: The conveyor's control panel has a word lock. Sprocket has stuck a note on it: 'What has lots of keys but can't open a single door? Answer me, and I'll give you MY key.'
hints: Listen: somewhere in the factory, a toy is playing a tune.
You play it with your fingers. It has black and white keys.
puzzles.solvedText: The panel pops open with a TING! Inside: the curly handle of a big wind-up key. Just the handle.

variants.prompt: The conveyor's control panel has a word lock. Sprocket has stuck a note on it: 'What has one eye but can't see a thing? Answer me, and I'll give you MY key.'
hints: Think about how teddy bears are stitched together.
You push thread through its eye.

variants.prompt: The conveyor's control panel has a word lock. Sprocket has stuck a note on it: 'What goes up and down but never moves? Answer me, and I'll give you MY key.'
hints: Think about how you got up to the factory floor.
You climb them one at a time.

puzzles.title: The Missing Key Rod
puzzles.prompt: The wind-up key's rod is hidden somewhere on the line. Search the pile of teddies, the toy chest and the foreman's stool.
hints: Three places on the assembly line each hide a clue.
Dig through the teddies, the toy chest and under the foreman's stool.
puzzles.solvedText: A rod from a teddy, a pin from the chest, and oil from under the stool: you slide the pin in and oil it. A wind-up key's rod!

puzzles.title: The Tin Soldier Parade
puzzles.prompt: Five tin soldiers must march in the right order: {items}. The drawer under the belt has a keypad: 'Each soldier's place, first in line is 1, in the order I list them.'
hints: Every phone has a clue. Share them all out loud.
Start with the one you're surest about, and try each place.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The soldiers salute and the drawer slides open. Inside: Sprocket's magnifier, for inspecting teeny-tiny screws.

puzzles.title: The Teddy Bear Tester
puzzles.prompt: A machine that squeezes teddy bears to test their squeak has jammed. Its reset box has a 3-digit lock. Each of you checked the tag on a different bear.
hints: Every phone holds one of the digits, written as a fact. Say them out loud, in order.
In order: {facts}.
puzzles.solvedText: The machine hums back to life. Squeak! Squeak! Squeak! Every teddy on the belt passes the test.

generator.pieceTemplate: The tag on your teddy bear says: the {ordinal} digit is {fact}.

puzzles.title: The Giant Robot
puzzles.prompt: A toy robot as big as a fridge blocks the way out, frozen mid-step. There's a keyhole in its back.
hints: Wind-up toys need winding, and your key is in two pieces.
Put the key handle and the key rod together, then use the wind-up key on the robot.
puzzles.solvedText: Crank, crank, crank! The robot beeps a happy tune and marches out of the way, straight into the paint shop.

puzzles.title: The Paint Mixer
puzzles.prompt: The paint mixer has a 3-digit lock. Sprocket's sign on it says: '{order}!'
hints: Each phone saw one colour of paint pot, and how many of them there were.
Read them in the sign's order: {order}.
puzzles.solvedText: The mixer swirls every colour together, then spits out a little paint tin. Plink! Something rattles inside.

generator.pieceTemplate: You counted the {color} paint pots on your shelf: there were {digit} of them.

puzzles.title: The Paint Code Chart
puzzles.prompt: Sprocket labels his paint pots in numbers so nobody else can read them. The newest one says: {cipher}. The chart's lock wants the colour's name.
hints: Each number is a letter.
A is 1, B is 2, C is 3… all the way to Z is 26.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Correct! The chart flips over. On the back: 'Paint shop rules: NO FUN. Signed, Sprocket.'

puzzles.title: The Colour Lights
puzzles.prompt: The panel of coloured bulbs flickers on. Each button lights its bulb and flips the ones beside it. Turn every light on to mix the perfect colour.
hints: Work from the top row down: fix each row using the buttons in the row below it.
Press {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Every bulb glows and the paint pots burble happily. Sprocket mutters: 'Beginner's luck.'

puzzles.title: The Painters' Coat Rack
puzzles.prompt: A little locked cupboard hangs under the coat rack. Its word lock has a riddle painted on it: 'I have a thumb and four fingers, but I'm not alive.'
hints: Look at what the painters wear to keep their hands clean.
You wear it on your hand.
puzzles.solvedText: The cupboard opens. Inside is a painted sign: 'Employee of the Month: SPROCKET'. He painted it himself.

variants.prompt: A little locked cupboard hangs under the coat rack. Its word lock has a riddle painted on it: 'What can you catch but never throw?'
hints: Achoo!
You might catch one in winter.

variants.prompt: A little locked cupboard hangs under the coat rack. Its word lock has a riddle painted on it: 'What has a head and a tail, but no body?'
hints: Look in the painters' pockets for spare change.
You flip it to decide heads or tails.

puzzles.title: The Gearbox
puzzles.prompt: The gearbox that runs the shipping dock is missing one golden gear. Without it, nothing moves.
hints: Something shiny was hiding in the paint tin, too small to see.
Look closely at the paint tin with the magnifier, then use the golden gear on the gearbox.
puzzles.solvedText: The gear clicks into place and the whole factory whirs. A printer beside the gearbox prints out a shipping label with your names on it!

puzzles.title: The Delivery Numbers
puzzles.prompt: The crate numbers go: {sequence}. The next crate's number is missing, and the dock's keypad wants it.
hints: Look at how each number changes to get the next one.
The next number is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Beep! The keypad lights green and the trolley rolls itself out of the way.

puzzles.title: The Parrot Crate
puzzles.prompt: A toy parrot is stuck inside a crate with a word lock. It squawks: 'Sprocket's three favourite toys, first to last! Squawk!'
hints: Three phones each remember one toy from Sprocket's list.
Say them in order, first to last, like: toy toy toy.
puzzles.solvedText: The crate pops open and the parrot flaps out: '{answer}! {answer}!' It lands on your shoulder and won't let go.

generator.pieceTemplate: You read it on a crate label: the {ordinal} toy on Sprocket's favourites list is the {word}.

puzzles.title: The Delivery Note
puzzles.prompt: A crumpled delivery note is in code: {cipher}. The driver's lock wants the word.
hints: How far to slide the letters is written somewhere. Check the driver's clipboard.
Slide every letter back along the alphabet by that many places.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The lock clicks. The note is a list of toys, all ready to be delivered to children.

puzzles.title: The Beeping Radio
puzzles.prompt: The dock radio beeps in dots and dashes: {cipher}
hints: These need a key. Sprocket wrote it too small to read without a magnifier.
Swap each one for its letter, one at a time.
puzzles.solvedText: The radio falls quiet. Sprocket grumbles: 'Who taught you Morse code?'

puzzles.title: The Loading Door
puzzles.prompt: The loading door needs the shipping label AND a 3-digit code. Sprocket's note: 'Robots on my assembly line, then mixers in my paint shop, then trucks at my dock!'
pieces: You counted the robots on the assembly line: 5.
You remember the paint shop: it had 2 mixers.
You counted the trucks waiting at the dock: 4.
hints: Three phones remember three numbers. Put them in the order on Sprocket's note.
Robots, then mixers, then trucks.
puzzles.solvedText: The label slides into the slot and the keypad plays a jolly jingle. With a clatter, the big door starts to roll up.

pieces: You counted the robots on the assembly line: 6.
You remember the paint shop: it had 1 mixer.
You counted the trucks waiting at the dock: 3.
You counted the robots on the assembly line: 8.
You remember the paint shop: it had 3 mixers.
You counted the trucks waiting at the dock: 5.
